steps.title: Reagent handling and storage
steps.instruction: Gather all listed reagents with the indicated catalog numbers and store them as specified: OCT (Sakura Finetek, cat 4583); 2‑methylbutane (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat M32631); Urea (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat U1250); Sodium deoxycholate (SDC, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat D6750); TCEP (Thermo Fisher, cat 77720), freshly prepared; Chloroacetamide (CAA, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat C0267); Protease inhibitor cocktail (PIC, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat P8340) – store at –20 °C in aliquots; Tris‑HCl (Sigma‑Aldrich, cat T5941); Ammonium bicarbonate (ABC, Sigma‑Aldrich, cat 09830); Sequencing‑grade trypsin (Promega, cat V5111) – store at –80 °C; reconstituted enzyme used immediately or stored at –20 °C short‑term; Lys‑C (Fujifilm Wako, cat 125‑05061) – store at –80 °C; Formic acid (FA, Fisher Scientific, cat A117‑50); iRT peptides (Biognosys, cat Ki3002); PBS (Thermo Fisher, cat 10010002); ceramic beads 1 mm and 3 mm (MP Biomedicals, cats 150010, 150030); Protein LoBind tubes (Eppendorf, cat 0030108116); 0.5 mL centrifuge tubes (Corning, cat 3208); 1.5 mL centrifuge tubes (Corning, cat 3620); pipette tips (Axygen, 10 µL T‑300‑L, 200 µL T‑200‑C‑L, 1 mL T‑1,000‑C); C18 SPE disks (3M Empore, cat 98060402173); PEN membrane slides (Zeiss, cat 415190‑9041‑000); opaque adhesive caps (Zeiss, cat 415190‑9181‑000); Ex kit (Omicsolution, cat OSFP004‑96).

steps.title: Prepare buffers and digestion mixes
steps.instruction: Make all buffers according to the recipes, using the reagents above.

substeps.instruction: Lysis buffer for bulk sample (final 1 mL): dissolve 480 mg urea to 8 M, add 50 mg SDC (1 % w/v), 100 µL 10 mM TCEP, 100 µL 40 mM CAA, 100 µL 1× PIC, and 500 µL 100 mM Tris‑HCl (1 M, pH 8.5). Adjust volume to 1 mL.
Lysis buffer for microdissected strips (final 1 mL): add 50 mg SDC (1 % w/v), 100 µL 10 mM TCEP, 100 µL 40 mM CAA, 100 µL 1× PIC, and 500 µL 50 mM Tris‑HCl (1 M, pH 8.5). Adjust volume to 1 mL.
Digestion buffer for bulk sample: add Lys‑C and trypsin to 100 mM ABC so that enzyme : substrate = 50 : 1 (wt/wt); keep on ice until use.
Digestion buffer for microdissected strips: prepare 50 mM ABC (pH 8.0) and add trypsin at 0.05 pg per µm³ tissue (pg/µm³).
Buffer A: 0.1 % formic acid in water.
Buffer B: 80 % acetonitrile with 0.1 % formic acid.

steps.title: Tissue preparation and sectioning
steps.instruction: Process mouse brain tissue and obtain frozen sections.

substeps.instruction: Take the brain of an 8‑week‑old female C57BL/6J mouse following approved ethical guidelines.
Rinse the brain with ice‑cold PBS and embed it in OCT compound.
Snap‑freeze the embedded brain in 2‑methylbutane pre‑cooled with liquid nitrogen.
Store the frozen blocks at –80 °C until sectioning; keep all handling on ice or at 4 °C to prevent protein degradation.
Pre‑cool the frozen block at –20 °C for 1 h and set the cryostat to –20 °C to –30 °C; cut 10‑µm‑thick horizontal sections.
Collect the sections onto PEN membrane slides.
Store the slides at –80 °C until laser microdissection.

steps.title: Laser microdissection of tissue strips
steps.instruction: Isolate eight adjacent strips from each section using the LMD system.

substeps.instruction: Set up the Leica LMD7000 system according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Capture an image of the whole‑brain slide with the microscope camera.
Select eight adjacent tissue slices for S4P sampling.
Define two anatomical feature points in each slice for angle alignment across adjacent slices.
For each slice, set a cutting direction that differs by 22.5° from the previous slice (total of eight angles).
Program the LMD to cut parallel strips 300 µm wide.
Collect the dissected strips into 200 µL opaque adhesive caps.
Verify successful collection under the microscope.

steps.title: Proteomic preparation of bulk tissue
steps.instruction: Lyse, digest, and clean up peptides from a bulk mouse brain sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL lysis buffer for bulk sample to mouse tissue placed in 0.5‑mL reinforced polypropylene tubes containing 1 mm and 3 mm ceramic beads.
Homogenize with an OMNI Bead Ruptor Elite (10 m/s, 2 cycles, 30 s on, 15 s off) and keep the tube on ice water.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C; transfer the supernatant to Protein LoBind tubes.
Add the digestion buffer for bulk sample; incubate at 37 °C with shaking at 1,000 rpm for 16 h.
Acidify the digest with formic acid to pH 2–3.
Purify peptides using self‑made C18 stage‑tips.
Dry the purified peptides in a SpeedVac and re‑constitute in 0.1 % formic acid.

steps.title: Proteomic preparation of microdissected strips
steps.instruction: Lyse, digest, and clean up peptides from the laser‑captured strips.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL lysis buffer for microdissected strips to each adhesive cap containing the tissue strips.
Invert the caps and incubate for 2 h at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 5,000 × g for 2 min; collect the lysate.
Add the digestion buffer for microdissected strips.
Purify the resulting peptides with the Ex kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Spike the peptide solution with iRT peptides for retention‑time calibration.
Dry the peptides in a SpeedVac and re‑constitute in 0.1 % formic acid (store at –20 °C for up to one week if needed).

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS analysis of peptides
steps.instruction: Separate and acquire mass spectra of the peptide samples.

substeps.instruction: Configure an Ultimate 3000 nanoLC system equipped with a 25 cm × 75 µm i.d. analytical column.

Set the flow rate to 300 nL/min and apply the following gradient: start at 4 % Buffer B / 96 % Buffer A, increase to 28 % B in 40 min, to 44 % B in 5 min, to 90 % B in 3 min, hold 3 min, decrease to 4 % B in 3 min, and hold 7 min.
Operate the timsTOF Pro in diaPASEF mode with 22 × 40 Th precursor isolation windows covering m/z 249–1229.
Set the collision‑energy ramp from 59 eV down to 20 eV across the ion‑mobility range.
Inject 200 ng of peptides per sample, using either the sliding‑window order or a randomized order to minimise batch effects.

steps.title: Data preprocessing of DIA runs
steps.instruction: Convert raw DIA files into quantitative protein tables.

substeps.instruction: Process the raw DIA data in Spectronaut 16.2 with default settings.
Search against the Mus musculus UniProt database (UP000000589).
Specify carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification; oxidation (M) and N‑terminal acetylation as variable modifications.
Apply a 1 % false‑discovery‑rate cutoff at both precursor and protein levels.
Normalize protein intensities in each strip sample by the non‑zero median value.
Export the normalized protein expression matrix as a CSV file (rows = proteins, columns = strip samples) and save a design matrix listing strip angles and positions.

steps.title: Spatial reconstruction with DeepS4P
steps.instruction: Reconstruct 2‑D protein distribution maps using the DeepS4P neural network.

substeps.instruction: Install Python packages: torch==1.13.1, numpy, and scipy.
Clone the DeepS4P repository from https://github.com/Ma-JC/DeepS4P.
Load the preprocessed protein expression CSV and the design matrix into the Python environment.
Configure the neural network: input layer 446 nodes; two hidden layers with 2,048 and 4,096 nodes respectively, using ReLU activation; output layer with 7,330 nodes.
Set loss‑function parameters: reconstruction weight = 1.0; L2 regularization λ = 0.001; sparsity weight α = 0.01; smoothness weight β = 0.1.
Train the model for 1,000 epochs using the Adam optimizer.
Apply a Gaussian filter with σ = 1 to the output for image smoothing and noise reduction.
Generate a spatial distribution map for each protein and save the results as .npy files or image files.
Adjust any of the above parameters as needed for different sample setups.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol has been used and validated in the following research article: Qin et al. [20]. In-depth and high-throughput spatial proteomics for whole-tissue slice profiling by deep learning-facilitated sparse sampling strategy. Cell Discovery (Figures 2–7, Supplementary figures S1–S15). Validation data include a comparison with immunohistochemistry staining for known regional markers (Figure 3a, Supplementary Figure S9), consistency with the gridding-based spatial proteomics approach (Supplementary Figure S2), reconstruction accuracy for marker proteins and spatially co-localized proteins (Figure 4), and reproducibility across technical and biological replicates (Figure 2, Supplementary Figure S4).
